subject: Science
title: Colours in nature
objectives: Children will find colours in nature on a walk.
Children will make a collage with natural materials.
content: Finding colours in nature on a walk, noticing the colours of flowers and leaves, and making a nature collage.
teachingActivities: Use colour cards on a walk; let children collect fallen items only; name each colour; link to colour words learnt in Literacy and Numeracy; accept all creative collages.
learnerActivities: Find colours in nature and make a collage with leaves and flowers.
resources: Colour cards: red, green, yellow, brown
assessment: Observe whether each child finds three colours in nature and makes a collage.
expectedOutcomes: Makes a collage with leaves or flowers.

lessons.title: Colour walk
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will find colours in nature on a walk.
successCriteria: Finds something that matches a colour card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name materials and sort natural and made things.
resources: Colour cards: red, green, yellow, brown
lessons.starter: Show the green card and say "Let us find something green in nature."
teacherActivities: Show each colour card and say its name.
Walk to the garden in a line with colour cards.
Say "Find something green" and let children search.
Find one thing for each colour.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the colour.
Child finds a green leaf and holds it to the card.
Child finds and names the colour.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each colour card and say its name. Children: Children look and say the colour.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk to the garden in a line with colour cards. Children: Children walk in a line.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Find something green" and let children search. Children: Child finds a green leaf and holds it to the card.
Step 4. Teacher: Find one thing for each colour. Children: Child finds and names the colour.

practical.title: Colour hunt
steps: Give each pair a colour card.
practical.safety: Check the area for sharp objects, thorns and insects first. Collect only fallen items and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point to something that matches.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two things for each colour.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects in a basket and say "Colours everywhere."
lessons.homeConnection: Look for colours in nature on a walk with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find colours in nature on a walk" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Colours of flowers and leaves
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will compare the colours of flowers and leaves.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name materials and sort natural and made things.
lessons.starter: Hold up a yellow flower and a green leaf and say "The flower is yellow. The leaf is green."
teacherActivities: Show different flowers and leaves and name the colours.
Look closely with a magnifying glass at the colours and patterns.
Sort the flowers and leaves by colour onto colour paper.
Ask "How many yellow things do we have?"
learnerActivities: Children look and say the colours.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show different flowers and leaves and name the colours. Children: Children look and say the colours.
Step 2. Teacher: Look closely with a magnifying glass at the colours and patterns. Children: Children look and point.
Step 3. Teacher: Sort the flowers and leaves by colour onto colour paper. Children: Child sorts by colour.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many yellow things do we have?" Children: Child counts with support.

practical.title: Colour sort
steps: Put coloured paper on the mat.
Sort flowers and leaves by colour.
practical.safety: Use only fallen leaves and flowers and wash hands after. Do not allow flowers in mouths.

differentiation.support: Offer two colours and say the colour first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find leaves that are not green.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts flowers and leaves by colour
lessons.conclusion: Put the flowers in a vase and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at the colours of flowers and leaves at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "compare the colours of flowers and leaves" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Making a nature collage
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will make a collage with natural materials.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name materials and sort natural and made things.
resources: Fallen leaves, petals, seeds and sticks
lessons.starter: Show a collage made of leaves and petals and say "We can make pictures from nature."
teacherActivities: Show how to put glue on paper and stick leaves.
Let each child choose natural things and stick them.
learnerActivities: Child sticks leaves and petals on paper.
Child says a word such as flower or tree.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put glue on paper and stick leaves. Children: Children watch and get glue.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child choose natural things and stick them. Children: Child sticks leaves and petals on paper.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What did you make?" Children: Child says a word such as flower or tree.
Step 4. Teacher: Display the collages together. Children: Child shows their collage.

practical.title: Nature collage
practical.safety: Use non-toxic glue and avoid small seeds for children who put things in their mouths. Wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Stick the leaf together and name the picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a collage of a tree with leaves.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes a collage with natural materials
lessons.conclusion: Put the collages on the wall and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Make a nature picture at home with leaves and paper.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a collage with natural materials" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Colour sorting game
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort natural objects and pictures by colour.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name materials and sort natural and made things.
resources: A mix of natural objects and pictures
lessons.starter: Say "I have a bag of nature things. Let us sort them by colour."
teacherActivities: Pick an object from the bag and say its colour.
Put it in the matching coloured basket.
Let each child pick an object and sort it.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the colour.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick an object from the bag and say its colour. Children: Children say the colour.
Step 2. Teacher: Put it in the matching coloured basket. Children: Children watch and say the colour.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick an object and sort it. Children: Child sorts by colour.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each basket together. Children: Children name the colours.

practical.title: Colour baskets
steps: Put coloured baskets on the mat.
Put it in the matching basket.
practical.safety: Use only safe, large objects. Supervise turns and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Offer two baskets and say the colour first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find an object that is two colours.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which basket does it go in?

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say the colours.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort things by colour at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort natural objects and pictures by colour" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 colours check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child finds colours in nature and makes a collage.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name materials and sort natural and made things.
lessons.starter: Sing the colour song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: colour sort, flowers and leaves, and collage.
At each station ask "What colour is it?" and "What did you make?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or gesture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: colour sort, flowers and leaves, and collage. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What colour is it?" and "What did you make?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Colour stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use non-toxic materials and wash hands.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two colours.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to describe their collage.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: finds colours in nature; sorts by colour; makes a collage.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
Finds and names colours in nature
lessons.homeConnection: Look for colours in nature each day.

What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
